chapter: Chicago radio, Whiteman and courting Mildred
title: The Three Spooks and a paid trip to Chicago
summary: At the station he led a piano, alto and xylophone trio; the manager grants two weeks' paid travel, and he describes the Marigold band's musicians.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: So, when it got near Spring, Kelfer was --

said to me, 'I'll tell you what, you been here awhile' and I used to do a late night program for them and everything, and we had a trio, called the Three Spooks. And, oh, what's his name, Pierre Andre was our announcer. You remember him in Chicago?
Yeah, well he started out with -- he was a shoe salesman, he tried out there.
Yeah, and John Wald came in after -- and funny, this Jack Tiboo got him a job with WGN. But I'm getting ahead of my story --
But your trio was what? Piano and bass? Or bass and drum?
Piano, alto and xylophone. No bass --

So, he said, I'll give you -- if you'll sign a year's contract, I'll give you two weeks with pay --he said, 'Take a trip,' He said, 'Where do you want to go?' He said, 'I'll buy your fare.' I said, 'I'm going to Chicago.' 'So I'll give you the money.' And, during that time I was there, (unintelli-
gible), my sister came and visited, my mother came, you know, we had-- there she came for the holidays and all. I was kind of happy there, it was nice, around good musicians for a --
OH, the band at the Marigold was a wonderful band.
Oh, yes. Fellas from the University of Minnesota, a lot of them. Just great players. And, couple of them later Whiteman even tried to get.
